text:
alex: Heads up — seeing a big tail-latency spike in eu-west-1 for text-gen requests starting ~1769059000. P95 jumped from 120ms -> 1.6s, P99 ~3.8s. Dashboard: https://console.internal/redwood/metrics?region=eu-west-1 :thinking_face:
priya: confirming, traces show KV cache miss rate spiked and batching latency rose. This started right after last runtime rollout (runtimes/v2.14). :exclamation:
jamie: logs from runtime nodes show frequent KV eviction warnings + 'batch queue size growth' messages. Attaching tail of node log snippet:
```
[2026-03-18T10:45:12Z] WARN kvcache: prefix_evicted key=acct_1234 len=4096
[2026-03-18T10:45:12Z] INFO batcher: queue_len=48 avg_wait_ms=120.3
[2026-03-18T10:45:13Z] ERROR runtime: rpc_handler latency=1587ms path=/v1/generate
```
marta: autoscaler started cordoning some GPU nodes in eu-west-1 due to OOMs last hour; capacity dropped ~22% which compounded the batching backlog. Node events: `OOMKilled` on cudnn kernel a few times.
ken: Is this the runtime change that adjusted dynamic batching thresholds? I remember there was a tweak in v2.14 to increase batch size for better throughput.
priya: yes — default max_batch_tokens increased from 2048 -> 4096 and kvcache retention dropped to 60s in the same PR. Looks like for short requests that hurts tail latency when capacity is constrained.
alex: we need emergency mitigations. Suggested actions: (1) disable dynamic batching (flip feature flag) (2) revert kvcache retention to 300s or enable per-customer pinning (3) shift new traffic away from eu-west-1 to eu-central-1 / dedicated pools.
jamie: I've prepared the patch to flip batching off in runtime config manager. Command to apply (will affect all hosts in eu-west-1 once config rollout completes):
```
# toggle feature flag
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' \
  https://controlplane.internal/flags/runtime.dynamic_batching \
  -d '{"value": false, "targets": ["eu-west-1"]}'
```
marta: on it. Also starting immediate node recycle for the 3 OOM nodes to bring healthy capacity back.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: flag change accepted — rollout scheduled to 3 groups, ETA ~45s per group. CI: OK.
ken: While we roll that, can we route new requests to dedicated capacity? I can open a traffic-shift policy to split 40% -> eu-central dedicated pools to take pressure off eu-west-1. That will increase cost but reduce risk.
alex: do it. Prioritize stability over cost for now. Set alert for cost blowout and we will revert when healthy.
priya: routing policy applied: `route-policy apply --from eu-west-1 --to eu-central:deds --pct 40 --sticky 5m` — CLI output: OK.
oncall-bot: alert: incident-eu-west-latency created. Severity: high. Pager notified.
jamie: monitoring shows p95 falling already to ~280ms in the first 2 minutes after batching flag change and routing. P99 still ~1.2s but trending down.
marta: kvcache retention revert queued — requires small runtime bump (hot-restart). I recommend we hold that until traffic stabilizes because restarts will drop active KV caches and might temporarily worsen tail — but retention change itself should help once nodes are healthy.
ken: agree. Let's stabilize first, then do retention revert with canary (10% traffic).
alex: good plan. Postmortem items: rollback policy review for batching changes, add canary for kvcache retention changes, update autoscaler thresholds for GPU OOM detection, and a runbook entry for rapid traffic-shift.
priya: adding to incident board. I'll keep watching metrics for 30m. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
